questions.q: What does de Grey say is the real cure for aging?
a: Repairing damage that has already accumulated
Preventing damage through a strict lifestyle
Taking medication for each symptom as it appears
Slowing the aging process with calorie restriction
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the solution is neither prevention nor medication but repairing the damage already done.

questions.q: Why is repair better than merely slowing aging?
a: It can be repeated and keep extending your lifespan
It works only once but permanently stops aging
It avoids the need for any future medical treatment
It restores the body to exactly its teenage state
questions.why: Lesson 1 says repaired damage can be treated again for the rest of your life, potentially extending lifespan to twice the expected age.

questions.q: What damage do mitochondrial free radicals cause?
a: They mutate mitochondrial DNA and speed up aging
They block nutrients from reaching the cell nucleus
They destroy the protective membrane around cells
They prevent mitochondria from producing any energy
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that free radicals produced in mitochondria can mutate mitochondrial DNA, which accelerates aging.

a: Hiding a backup of mitochondrial DNA in the nucleus
Removing damaged mitochondria from every cell
Injecting healthy mitochondria into the bloodstream
Slowing the production of free radicals with drugs
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes allotopic expression as storing a healthy copy of mitochondrial DNA in the protected nucleus.

questions.q: What mindset change does de Grey call for?
a: Accepting risk and some deaths to speed up approvals
Waiting for perfect safety data before any human trials
Focusing funding on prevention rather than repair
Treating aging as a natural process beyond medicine
questions.why: Lesson 3 says exaggerating every failed treatment creates delays, and accepting some risk could save more lives overall.
